title: A Multivariate Copula Framework for Joint Modeling of Ranking Concordance, Dispersion, and Extremeness
content: Ranking analysis underpins decisions in many areas, from peer review to sports. Standard evaluation methods examine concordance, dispersion, and extremeness separately, often ignoring their interdependencies. This assumption risks biased inferences and a partial view of ranking patterns. The Concordance-Dispersion-Extremity Framework (CDEF) offers a new copula-based approach that jointly models these dimensions. Using Gumbel copulas to capture multivariate dependence, CDEF combines Kendall’s W (concordance), concentration measures (hypergeometric or multinomial, selected via chi-square tests), and Gumbel extreme value distributions (extremeness). Monte Carlo estimation enables practical computation of the joint probabilities. Applying CDEF to NCAA football rankings showed striking differences from traditional univariate assessments. Standard methods indicated strong ranking properties—high concordance (Kendall’s W=0.717), significant concentration, and pronounced extremeness. However, the copula-based model revealed that these effects largely diminish when dependencies are accounted for (P(Concordance|Dispersion,Extremeness)=0.091). Much of the perceived agreement arose from shared patterns, not genuine consensus. CDEF thus advances ranking analysis by revealing how apparent strength in one dimension depends on the others. This richer perspective helps detect bias, assess reliability, and support sound decisions in settings where rankings have serious consequences. Ignoring dependence can foster unwarranted confidence in ranking systems, highlighting the need for approaches that model these relationships explicitly.
